info.name: Chaos Mage Homebrew
info.description: Chaos Mage class for Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition.
info.author: Homebrew

description.p: A Chaos Mage channels primordial chaos rather than controlling magic through study, bloodline, or divine authority. Their magic is powerful, unstable, and alive with possibility. Every spell passes through the Witch’s Coin: every spell might remain stable, or become something more.

ul.li: Hit Dice: 1d6 per Chaos Mage level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 6 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per Chaos Mage level after 1st
Skills: Choose two from Arcana, Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

description.p: You begin with the following equipment:

ul.li: (a) a quarterstaff or (b) any simple weapon
(a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
(a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus
(a) a scholar’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack
Leather armor and your Witch’s Coin

Ability Score Improvement, Chaos Burn Stage II Available
Manifestation Feature, Chaos Burn Stage IV Available
Absolute Chaos, Chaos Burn Stage V Available
Master of Chaos, Chaos Burn Stage VI Available

sheet.description: A spellcaster who channels primordial chaos through the Witch’s Coin.

setters.set: A spellcaster who channels primordial chaos through the Witch’s Coin.

description.p: Charisma is your spellcasting ability. You follow the Sorcerer’s spell slot progression and spells-known progression. You may learn spells from the Sorcerer spell list, the Chaos Mage spell list, and selected healing spells from the Cleric and Druid spell lists. The additional lists will be added in the Chaos Mage spell content.
Your Witch’s Coin is your required spellcasting focus. You must flip it whenever you cast a spell or cantrip, as described in the Witch’s Coin feature.

Your magic leaves unmistakable signs of primordial chaos. Whenever you cast a spell, its appearance may be accompanied by purple-black fractures in the air, sickly green sparks, your shadow moving incorrectly, your voice briefly echoing with another voice, or reality rippling around your hands. These manifestations are cosmetic unless another feature says otherwise.

The Witch’s Coin is the heart of Chaos Mage spellcasting and your required spellcasting focus. Whenever you cast any spell or cantrip, regardless of where you gained that spell, you must flip the Witch’s Coin.
Heads — Stable Reality. The spell functions normally.
Tails — Chaos Mutation. The spell functions normally but also triggers a Chaos Mutation.

Timing: Cast the spell, expend all required resources, flip the coin, determine a mutation on Tails, then resolve the spell with its mutation. Each spell normally triggers only one flip, regardless of concentration, number of targets, number of attacks, duration, or repeated damage. A Chaos spell may specifically override this rule. One spell produces one mutation affecting the spell as a whole.

The coin is a physical object bound specifically to you. To anyone else, it is an ordinary coin. If lost, stolen, or destroyed, you may perform a 1-hour ritual to create and bind a replacement. Without your Witch’s Coin, you cannot cast spells or cantrips.

At character creation, choose whether you or the DM flips and rolls for the Witch’s Coin. This choice remains locked for the life of that character. Whoever flips the coin also makes the associated Chaos Mutation rolls.

At 2nd level, you gain a pool of Chaos Points. Your maximum equals your Chaos Mage level + your Charisma modifier. You regain all expended Chaos Points when you finish a long rest. Chaos Points cannot normally fall below 0.
Gamble Again (1 point). After determining a Chaos Mutation result, reroll it. You must use the new result.
Intensify Mutation (2 points). Roll twice when determining the Chaos Mutation effect and choose either result.
Stabilize Chaos (2 points). Ignore one harmful effect caused by the Chaos Mutation.
Spread Chaos (3 points). If the spell normally targets only one creature, the mutation may also affect one additional eligible creature within the spell’s range.

You may combine different Chaos Point abilities on the same spell if you can pay their full costs, but cannot use the same ability more than once on the same spell unless another feature says otherwise. These abilities are used after the coin is flipped. If there is no mutation, mutation-based abilities cannot be used.

Overdrawing Chaos. Once per long rest, you may activate a Chaos Point ability even if you cannot fully afford its cost. Your Chaos Points become 0. The DM determines the consequences, which may involve Chaos Burn.

You have advantage on saving throws caused by your own spells, your own Chaos Mutations, and your own Chaos Mage effects.

At 3rd level, choose how primordial chaos manifests through you: Manifestation of Creation, Manifestation of Mutation, Manifestation of Ruin, or Manifestation of Transformation. Your Manifestation grants features at levels 3, 6, 14, and 18.

When your Witch’s Coin lands on Tails, you gain 1 temporary Chaos Point. This temporary point may only be spent on a Chaos Point ability affecting that spell’s Chaos Mutation. If it is not spent before the spell resolves, it disappears. You may gain this temporary Chaos Point only once per turn.

When a Chaos Mutation triggers, you may spend 3 Chaos Points. Before determining the Chaos Effect, shift the Chaos Category one step higher or lower. You then roll three Chaos Effect results from the chosen category and select one.

Once per long rest, when your Witch’s Coin lands on Tails, you may allow the mutation to echo. After the first Chaos Mutation resolves, roll a second Chaos Effect from the same Chaos Category. Both effects apply to the spell.

When casting a spell or cantrip, you may spend 1 Chaos Point to treat the Witch’s Coin as though it landed on Tails without flipping it. The spell automatically triggers a Chaos Mutation.

When you have 0 Chaos Points, you may continue using Will of the Witch without limit. Each use while at 0 Chaos Points requires a Chaos Burn Check: roll 1d100 for a Chaos Roll and 1d100 for a Burn Roll. If the Chaos Roll is lower than the Burn Roll, you gain 1 Chaos Burn.

When another creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell or cantrip, you may use your reaction and spend 2 Chaos Points to force its spell through your Witch’s Coin. Flip normally. On Heads, the spell resolves normally. On Tails, the spell triggers a Chaos Mutation as though you had cast it. The original caster retains control of the spell’s normal targets and choices. You are considered the source of the Chaos Mutation for your Chaos Mage abilities. Borrowed Chaos may affect allied or hostile spellcasters.

Once per long rest, when your Witch’s Coin lands on Tails and triggers a Chaos Mutation, you may invoke Chaos Dominion and choose one:
Dominion of Effect. Apply the Chaos Mutation to two separate valid creatures, objects, or areas within the original spell’s range, provided the mutation can logically affect both.
Primordial Recovery. Regain expended Chaos Points equal to your Charisma modifier.

Primordial Recovery. Regain expended Chaos Points equal to your Charisma modifier.

Once per long rest, when a Chaos Mutation occurs, you may maximize one numerical aspect of that mutation: damage, number of targets, duration, or area of effect. For the chosen aspect, use the maximum value permitted by the mutation instead of rolling or using its normal variable value.

Your maximum Chaos Points increase by 5. When you roll initiative with fewer than 5 Chaos Points, regain enough to reach 5. Will of the Witch costs 0 Chaos Points. Once per turn when you trigger a Chaos Mutation, you may reroll either its Chaos Category or its Chaos Effect and choose which result to use. You may unlock Chaos Burn Stage VI.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
